query: Agar consideration unlawful ho to kya contract void hai?
expected_answer: Agreement is void if consideration or object is unlawful, forbidden by law, or fraudulent.

query: What makes an agreement void for unlawful consideration under Contract Act?
expected_answer: Consideration or object is unlawful if forbidden by law, defeats provisions of law, fraudulent, or immoral.

query: What is the effect of coercion, fraud or misrepresentation on a contract?
expected_answer: Voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused.

query: When is compensation payable for breach of contract where penalty is stipulated?
expected_answer: Party complaining is entitled to receive reasonable compensation not exceeding the penalty stipulated.

query: Is an agreement in restraint of trade void under Pakistani law?
expected_answer: Every agreement by which anyone is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business is to that extent void.

query: What happens if an agreement is made without consideration under Contract Act?
expected_answer: An agreement made without consideration is void unless expressed in writing and registered or promise to compensate for past voluntary services.

query: What is communication, acceptance and revocation of proposals?
expected_answer: Communication of proposals, acceptance, and revocation are deemed to be made by any act or omission.

query: Who are the persons competent to contract according to the Contract Act?
expected_answer: Every person competent to contract who is of the age of majority, sound mind, and not disqualified from contracting.

query: What is a contingent contract defined under Section 31?
expected_answer: A contract to do or not to do something, if some event, collateral to such contract, does or does not happen.

query: When is an agreement void on grounds of impossibility under Contract Act?
expected_answer: An agreement to do an act impossible in itself is void; doctrine of frustration.

query: What is the punishment for qatl-i-amd under Section 302 PPC?
expected_answer: Qatl-i-amd is punished with death as qisas, death or imprisonment for life as ta'zir, or imprisonment up to 25 years.

query: What constitutes the offence of theft under Section 378 of PPC?
expected_answer: Whoever intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without consent.

query: What is the definition of criminal conspiracy under Section 120A PPC?
expected_answer: When two or more persons agree to do or cause to be done an illegal act or an act by illegal means.

query: What is the punishment for cheating under Section 420 PPC?
expected_answer: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and fine.

query: What is defaming a deceased person or imputation of defamation under Section 499?
expected_answer: Whoever by words or signs makes or publishes any imputation concerning any person intending to harm reputation.

query: Under Section 300 PPC, how is qatl-i-amd defined?
expected_answer: Whoever, with the intention of causing death or bodily injury likely to cause death, causes the death of a person.

query: What is the punishment for kidnapping or abducting under Section 364A PPC?
expected_answer: Punished with death or imprisonment for life or rigorous imprisonment up to fourteen years.

query: What is hurt defined under Section 332 of the Pakistan Penal Code?
expected_answer: Whoever causes pain, harm, disease, infirmity or injury to any person causes hurt.

query: What is the right of private defence of the body under Section 100 PPC?
expected_answer: The right of private defence of the body extends to the voluntary causing of death in cases of reasonable apprehension of death or grievous hurt.

query: What is extortion under Section 383 of Pakistan Penal Code?
expected_answer: Intentionally putting any person in fear of any injury and dishonestly inducing delivery of property.

query: What does Article 25 of the Constitution say about equality of citizens?
expected_act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
expected_answer: All citizens are equal before law and are entitled to equal protection of law. There shall be no discrimination on basis of sex.

query: What is the fundamental right to fair trial under Article 10A of the Constitution?
expected_act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
expected_answer: For determination of civil rights or in criminal charge, a person shall be entitled to fair trial and due process.

query: What is the right to information under Article 19A of the Constitution?
expected_act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
expected_answer: Every citizen shall have the right to have access to information in all matters of public importance.

query: What protection is granted against retrospective punishment under Article 12?
expected_act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
expected_answer: No law shall authorize the punishment of a person for an act or omission that was not punishable at the time.

query: What does Article 9 of the Constitution guarantee regarding security of person?
expected_act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
expected_answer: No person shall be deprived of life or liberty save in accordance with law.

query: What is the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 184(3)?
expected_act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
expected_answer: Supreme Court has jurisdiction in matters of public importance with reference to enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

query: What does Article 4 guarantee to citizens regarding protection of law?
expected_act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
expected_answer: To enjoy the protection of law and to be treated in accordance with law is an inalienable right of every citizen.

query: What does Article 14 guarantee regarding dignity of man and privacy of home?
expected_act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
expected_answer: The dignity of man and, subject to law, the privacy of home, shall be inviolable.

query: What is freedom of trade, business or profession under Article 18?
expected_act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
expected_answer: Subject to regulation by licensing, every citizen has the right to enter upon any lawful profession or trade.

query: What is the appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 185?
expected_act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
expected_answer: Supreme Court has jurisdiction to hear and determine appeals from judgments, decrees, final orders or sentences of High Courts.

query: What is the procedure for recording FIR under Section 154 of CrPC?
expected_answer: Information relating to commission of a cognizable offence given to an officer in charge of a police station shall be reduced to writing.

query: When can police arrest without warrant under Section 54 of CrPC?
expected_answer: Any police officer may without warrant arrest any person who has been concerned in any cognizable offence.

query: What is the provision for grant of bail in non-bailable offences under Section 497 CrPC?
expected_answer: When any person accused of non-bailable offence is arrested, he may be released on bail unless reasonable grounds to believe guilty of death or imprisonment for life.

query: What is the power of the High Court or Sessions Court regarding bail under Section 498 CrPC?
expected_answer: High Court or Court of Session may direct that any person be admitted to bail or that bail required by police officer or Magistrate be reduced.

query: How is search of place entered by person sought to be arrested conducted under Section 47 CrPC?
expected_answer: Person residing in or in charge of place shall allow ingress and afford reasonable facilities for search.

query: What is the principle of res judicata under Section 11 of CPC?
expected_answer: No Court shall try any suit or issue in which the matter directly and substantially in issue has been directly and substantially in issue in a former suit.

query: What suits are barred by jurisdiction under Section 9 of CPC?
expected_answer: The Courts shall have jurisdiction to try all suits of a civil nature excepting suits of which their cognizance is expressly or impliedly barred.

query: What are the powers of court to grant temporary injunction under CPC Section 94 / Order 39?
expected_answer: In order to prevent the ends of justice from being defeated, the Court may grant a temporary injunction.

query: What is restitution under Section 144 of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908?
expected_answer: Where decree or order is varied or reversed in appeal or revision, court shall cause restitution to be made.

query: What are the inherent powers of civil court saved under Section 151 CPC?
expected_answer: Nothing in this Code shall limit or affect inherent power of Court to make such orders as necessary for ends of justice or to prevent abuse of process.

query: Can a suit for recovery of possession of immovable property be filed under Section 9 of Specific Relief Act?
expected_answer: Person dispossessed without consent of immovable property otherwise than in due course of law may recover possession by suit.

query: Under Section 12 of Specific Relief Act, when is specific performance enforceable?
expected_answer: Specific performance of contract may be enforced when act agreed to be done is in performance of trust or no standard exists for ascertaining damage.

query: Under Section 21 of Specific Relief Act, what contracts cannot be specifically enforced?
expected_answer: Contracts for which non-performance compensation in money is an adequate relief or contract running into minute details cannot be specifically enforced.

query: What is a declaratory decree under Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act?
expected_answer: Any person entitled to any legal character or to any right as to any property may institute a suit for declaration.

query: When is perpetual injunction granted under Section 54 of Specific Relief Act?
expected_answer: Perpetual injunction may be granted to prevent breach of an obligation existing in favor of applicant.

query: What is the legal procedure for registration of marriages under Section 5 of MFLO 1961?
expected_answer: Every marriage solemnized under Muslim Law shall be registered in accordance with provisions of this Ordinance.

query: What is the mandatory procedure for Talaq notice under Section 7 of Muslim Family Laws Ordinance?
expected_answer: Any man wishing to divorce his wife shall give notice in writing to Chairman of Union Council and supply copy to wife.

query: Under Section 6 of MFLO, what is required before contracting a polygamous marriage?
expected_answer: No man shall contract another marriage without previous permission in writing of the Arbitration Council.

query: What constitutes the offence of money laundering under Section 3 of AML Act 2010?
expected_answer: A person is guilty of money laundering if he acquires, converts, conceals or transfers property knowing it is proceeds of crime.

query: What is the punishment for money laundering under Section 4 of AML Act 2010?
expected_answer: Rigorous imprisonment for not less than one year up to ten years, and fine which may extend to five million rupees and forfeiture of property.
